applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision between the challenger's chain and the defender's chain, so K-C governs how that chain-against-chain collision is weighed.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse': whether the judge may fault a footed chain because a cited verse does not explicitly name Joseph, or must weigh the chains only by footing; I read K-C as forbidding the explicit-naming fault.
why: The judge faults the challenger's footed chain for not naming Joseph, which is a verse-level explicit-statement requirement rather than weighing the two chains by footing as K-C requires.
